summary: Defines the Authenticated Received Chain protocol, giving an authenticated chain of custody for an email so each handler can see earlier handlers and what their authentication checks found. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: Each mail handler signs a note saying what checks the message passed, so the next can trust it.

subtitle: A chain of signed header fields that lets each mail handler record what authentication checks the message passed.

tldr.problem: Mailing lists, scanning services and other intermediaries often modify messages or re-route them, which breaks SPF and DKIM and can make DMARC reject legitimate mail.
tldr.mechanism: Each ARC-enabled handler adds an ARC Set of three header fields (AAR, AMS, AS) that records its authentication assessment and signs it, extending an ordered chain that later handlers can validate.
tldr.outcome: A receiver can use a validated chain to inform its disposition decisions. ARC is Experimental, and the RFC says it fails if it opens significant new abuse vectors.

facts.label: DNS queries to validate N sets

today: RFC 8617 is Experimental and has not been obsoleted or updated. It builds on DKIM (RFC 6376) and Authentication-Results (RFC 8601).

sections.title: The Problem ARC Addresses
sections.content:
Email authentication such as SPF (RFC 7208) and DKIM (RFC 6376) is weakened when intermediate handlers process the message. DMARC (RFC 7489) relies on SPF and DKIM, so failures caused by intermediaries can make legitimate mail get rejected or misdirected.

Authenticated Received Chain (ARC) lets each Internet Mail Handler add its authentication assessment to an ordered set. The assessment is wrapped in a DKIM signature derivative, so later handlers can verify each assertion and the order of the whole set. The RFC borrows ideas from evidence collection: the assessment is the evidence, a handler taking the message is a custodian, and the whole set is a chain of custody.
sections.eli5: When a letter is opened and resealed along the way, the first stamp no longer matches. ARC lets each helper leave a signed note about what the stamp looked like when they got it.

sections.title: The Three ARC Header Fields
sections.content:
An ARC Set is three header fields that share one instance value i=. ARC-Authentication-Results (AAR) records the authentication assessment at arrival. It is like Authentication-Results (RFC 8601) plus an instance tag, and it MUST combine all results from the participating domain.

ARC-Message-Signature (AMS) has the same syntax as a DKIM-Signature, except that it has no version tag and its i tag is replaced by the instance tag. It SHOULD cover the message including the handler's modifications, MUST NOT cover Authentication-Results or any ARC header field, and SHOULD include existing DKIM-Signature fields.

ARC-Seal (AS) signs the ARC header fields, not the body. It uses only relaxed header canonicalization, allows only the tags i, a, b, d, s, t and a new cv tag, and an h tag MUST result in a cv status of fail. Instance values range from 1 to 50, and a valid set has exactly one of each field per instance.
sections.eli5: Each helper attaches three things: a note of what they checked, a signature on the letter, and a seal that ties their note to everyone's earlier notes.

sections.title: How Sealers and Validators Act
sections.content:
To seal a message, a Sealer first makes all its modifications, including any new DKIM-Signature. If the most recent AS already says cv=fail, it stops. Otherwise the instance is one more than the highest found, or 1 if there is no chain, and the Sealer attaches AAR, AMS and AS. The AS covers the ARC Set values in increasing instance order, and within a set the order is AAR, AMS, AS. Any handler MAY seal, whether or not it changed the message.

A Validator collects the sets. With none, the Chain Validation Status is none. With more than 50, or a broken structure, or a failing newest AMS, or any failing AS, it is fail. Otherwise it is pass. The cv value of instance 1 MUST be none and later ones MUST be pass. An optional step finds the oldest-pass value. All failures, including DNS failures, are permanent, and a broken chain cannot be continued. A failing chain MUST be treated as if there were no chain. A validator MAY signal failure in the SMTP exchange with status 5.7.29.
sections.eli5: A helper checks every note and seal from the first one to the last. If any is wrong, the whole trail is thrown out and nobody can add to it again.

sections.title: Use Cases
sections.content:
Authentication breaks in several common setups. Message-scanning services rewrite content and re-route mail, which breaks DKIM and SPF. Large sites with several tiers of mail servers can lose authentication data between tiers. Mailing lists repost messages to subscribers. In each case the handler can seal the message so the next domain sees the original assessment.

A receiving domain can also use the chain to see which ARC-enabled handlers break authentication. DMARC processors MAY, as local policy, accept the assessments in a chain when deciding if a message is DMARC compliant. A DMARC report can then mention the influence with the reason local_policy and include the chain status, the domain and selector for each AS, and the originating IP address from the first ARC Set.
sections.eli5: A mailing list that reposts your message changes it. With ARC, the list can say, "it looked fine to me when it arrived", and the next stop can decide whether to believe that.

sections.title: Security and Experimental Questions
sections.content:
ARC makes no claims about message content and does not judge whether a handler is trustworthy, only who handled the message. Recipients are told to treat messages with chains, and every Sealer, with suspicion, so a malicious actor cannot seal spam to help its delivery. Validating a chain of N sets can take up to 2*N DNS queries, which an attacker could exploit for load, and replaying an intact passing chain to many recipients costs extra lookups and signature checks. Header growth may also trouble older MTAs.

The RFC calls ARC a success if chains allow equal or better delivery of legitimate mail than heuristics, and a failure if it enables significant new abuse. Open questions include whether the AS adds value beyond the AMS, the DNS overhead of long chains and the use of multiple selectors. IANA registered the three header fields, the "arc" authentication method and the X.7.29 status code.
sections.eli5: A signed note proves who wrote it, not that they are honest. Checking a long trail also means doing a lot of lookups, so it can be used to slow someone down.
